title: Condon and McKenzie's record date and McKenzie's salesmanship
summary: Freeman recalls his first record, made at 21 with Condon and McKenzie, and how McKenzie and Condon could sell to record companies.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And on the strength of, there again, of a record I was to make a year later --now, I was 20, playing tenor and at the age of 21, Condon and McKenzie had the record date in Chicago, and I had played a lot of different things around Chicago.
That was the Blue Blowers. Mountain City-- Mound
Well, I never played with the Mountain City Blue Blowers, but McKenzie was there with them, and McKenzie was the kind of man who could sell things.

Musicians were never people who could go -- jazz musicians could never go call up a man who ran a recording company and sell themselves. Condon could do it, McKenzie could do it, as they were later to prove.
But anyway, here now was my first record, as I mentioned --
